items.before:
A BASE II processing center acting in support of one or more issuers. The
processing center processes completed account holder transactions (local
and interchange) for account holder account posting and billing. For
completed interchange transactions, the center is also responsible for
receiving and processing incoming transactions for the account holders of
the issuer or issuers.
items.after:
A BASE II processing center acting in support of one or more issuers.
The processing center processes completed cardholder transactions (local
and interchange) for cardholder account posting and billing. For completed
interchange transactions, the center is also responsible for receiving and
processing incoming transactions for the cardholders of the issuer or issuers.
items.reason: El cambio modifica el término 'account holder' por 'cardholder' y 'account posting' por 'cardholder account posting', lo que altera el significado de negocio en el contexto de los procesos de facturación y procesamiento.

items.before:
A numeric value used to define issuing processing. Multiple Issuing BINs can
be linked to the same Issuing Identifier in Visa's systems.
items.after:
A numeric value used to define issuing processing. It is not governed by ISO
and does not have to start with a four (4). Multiple issuing BINs can be linked
to the same issuing identifier within Visa systems, which can allow mirroring
of processing or routing configurations.
items.reason: El texto nuevo especifica que el Issuing Identifier no está gobernado por ISO y no debe comenzar con un 4, lo que modifica su definición comercial.

details.text: A Visa Point of Service (POS) merchandise return authorization message is used to notify an issuer in real time that a merchant return or credit voucher transaction is being processed to a specific account. The return amount is debited to the acquirer and is credited to the issuer. Code 20 in the first two positions of Field 3—Processing Code distinguishes returns from other 0100 request messages. A return is initiated at the POS. Use of the same terminal or merchant outlet used for the original purchase is not required. The return amount must be equal to or less than the amount of the original purchase. Returns for less than the amount of the original purchase occur when the cardholder returns only a portion of the goods originally purchased. Merchandise return authorization messages must not be used for reversing Account Funding Transactions (AFTs) or quasi cash transactions. Chip cards are valid for 0100 merchandise return authorization transactions. If the issuer is unavailable, STIP responds to the 0100 Merchant Return Authorization request and creates a 0120 advice for the issuer. Merchandise return reversals are forwarded to the issuer online. If an issuer is unavailable, 0400 Merchandise Return reversals are processed in STIP and a 0420 Merchandise Return reversal advice is sent to the issuer. The return amount must be equal to or less than the amount of the original purchase. If the issuer has opted to receive 0100 merchandise returns and the issuer is unavailable, 0100 merchandise returns are processed in STIP, and an 0120 merchandise return advice is sent to the issuer. If the issuer has opted to receive 0100 merchandise returns, merchandise return reversals are forwarded to issuers online. When an issuer is unavailable, 0400 merchandise return reversals are processed in STIP, and an 0420 merchandise return reversal advice is sent to the issuer.
